Subject: Request: adjacency matrix + egress policy for on‑prem VPC deployment

Hi Naomi / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare the internal ops work for our staging colo, the security and netops teams asked for two artifacts we don’t yet have in one place: a service adjacency matrix (which services need to talk to which Redwood runtime/control endpoints) and an egress policy catalog (IP/port destination list + recommended NAT/failover behavior).

Can you provide a consolidated matrix and any reference diagrams you are recommending for a private deployment (control plane <-> data plane demarc, shared services, and egress points)? Our timeline: staging acceptance next Friday (2026‑11‑13). If you can share a draft by EOD Monday 11/09, we’ll circulate to netops/security and surface any blockers.

Attachments: none from our side.

Appreciate it —
James Park
Infrastructure Lead, Acme Labs
james.park@acmelabs.com

Subject: Re: Request: adjacency matrix + egress policy for on‑prem VPC deployment

James — thanks for the clear ask.

We put together a first pass of what you described and want feedback on two things before we lock the final artifacts:

1) Service adjacency matrix (spreadsheet) — lists Redwood control endpoints (auth, model registry, telemetry ingestion, health APIs) vs runtime components (inference nodes, router/proxy, cache nodes). Column for required port/protocol, optional TLS termination notes, and recommended L3/L4 ACL entries.
2) Egress policy catalog (PDF) — grouping by purpose: control plane telemetry/metrics, model downloads, license checks, CDN for weights, and optional telemetry sinks. It includes suggested CIDR/port pairs and NAT/failover guidance.

I attached the two files: vpc-adjacency-matrix-v1.xlsx and egress-policy-catalog-v1.pdf. They are draft; we expect a short review loop with your netops team.

Proposed timeline:
- Mon 11/09 — you share netops/security comments
- Wed 11/11 — we update and add a small runbook section for failover testing
- Thu 11/12 — joint runbook dry run (30–45m)

Quick questions:
- Do you use an active NAT pair (primary/secondary) per colo or a shared egress pool across tenants?
- Any existing enterprise firewall/proxy (URL filtering) that will require us to use an outbound proxy?

Thanks — attaching the drafts now.

—
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: adjacency matrix + egress policy for on‑prem VPC deployment

Adding a couple of operational notes re: egress/NAT that we should call out in the catalog: 

- If Acme uses a single shared egress pool, we recommend tag‑based routing from inference subnets to a dedicated egress gateway. That lets netops apply per‑tenant SNAT mapping in a deterministic way and keeps runtime routing simple.
- For NAT failover, we prefer active/standby with floating IPs for predictable session behavior (model downloads during cold starts can be large and need continuity).
- If the outbound path includes an enterprise proxy for URL filtering, add proxy host/port to the egress-policy catalog and include certificate pinning notes for downloads of model artifacts.

Also linking the shared services catalog we maintain (internal drive link) — it maps common services (DNS, cert manager, statsd) to recommended placement (control plane vs local tenant).

On Mon we can sync with your netops folks; I can take the port matrix review.

Thanks — quick ops checklist I added to the catalog (see egress-policy-catalog-v1.pdf):

- Verify outbound ACLs for control plane endpoints: 443 to registry.redwood.com, 8443 to telemetry.ingest.redwood.com
- Confirm DNS resolution and split‑horizon entries for model registry hostnames (avoid public weight pulls when using mirrored registry)
- Run model download smoke: curl/sha256 check against s3 mirror before enabling cache priming
- NAT failover test: bring down primary NAT for 60s and validate session resumption for a 10MB artifact pull

James — if you can grant netops a short session Monday we’ll walk the adjacency sheet row‑by‑row and capture any non‑standard mappings.

FYI I also created a JIRA for followups: NETOPS-438.
